title: This human body is your chance
hook: bhaee paraapat maanukh dehureeaa: you have this human body; now is your chance (Asa M5, ang 12)

segments.voice: Yesterday, moh, and your line, out of the mud. Did you reach for one steady person? Tonight, the last So Purakh shabad, and it's about time. Day four hundred twelve.

A crowded government office. You took a paper ticket an hour ago: number 147. The screen says 139. You scroll your phone, check the time, scroll again. 143. You go to get water. 145. You answer a message from your cousin. And then you look up and the screen says 149, and a voice is calling a number that isn't yours anymore. Your turn came, and passed, while you were looking somewhere else. Guru Arjan uses that very idea, a turn. Today: maanukh.
screen: `TICKET 147. THE SCREEN SAYS 139.` → `SCROLLING, WATER, A MESSAGE.` → `THE SCREEN SAYS 149.`

segments.voice: The fourth So Purakh shabad is by Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru. It opens: bhaee paraapat maanukh dehureeaa. You have received this human body. Then: gobind milan kee eh teree bareeaa. This is your turn to meet the Lord of the universe. Bareeaa is a turn, like a turn in a queue, or your turn at the well. Sikh teaching speaks of the soul passing through many lives, and of a human birth as rare and precious, the one in which a person can consciously remember the One. So the shabad says, in paraphrase: other work won't help you here. Join the company of the holy and meditate on the Name alone. Put your effort into crossing the frightening ocean of the world; your life is slipping away in the color of maya. Notice it doesn't say other work is evil. Sikhs work, raise families and run businesses; Sikh tradition remembers Guru Arjan building the Harmandir Sahib. It says other work can't do this particular job. Then, like Guru Nanak yesterday, Guru Arjan turns humble. I haven't practiced meditation, austerity, self-control or right living, he says. I haven't served the holy or known the Lord. Nanak says: my deeds are lowly. I have come to Your shelter; protect my honor. So the chance isn't something to earn by being impressive. It's a turn that's already come. The number on the screen is yours, right now. Now is the chance.
screen: `MAANUKH DEHUREEAA: THIS HUMAN BODY.` · `BAREEAA: YOUR TURN TO MEET THE LORD.` · `OTHER WORK CAN'T DO THIS ONE JOB.` · `MY DEEDS ARE LOWLY; I SEEK YOUR SHELTER.` · then, large: `NOW IS THE CHANCE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: do today's good now. Think of one good thing you've been meaning to do: a call to someone lonely, an apology, a donation, a thank-you note. Something small enough to start today. Picture yourself doing it. Then decide when, exactly, today, you'll begin, and if you can, take the first tiny step as soon as the bell ends. For now, rest with the breath, and with the line: this is your turn. If you pray, you can say Waheguru once. The bell holds the time.
Maanukh, human: Guru Arjan says this human life is your turn to meet the Lord, so don't let it pass.
Your line: now is the chance. Today, the next time you catch yourself saying later, ask whether this is your number being called. Day four hundred twelve.

howItsDone: Bhaee paraapat is the last shabad of the So Purakh group in Rehras Sahib, recited each evening; its opening line is quoted in Sikh teaching about the preciousness of human life.

pairs: the fifth Guru, the voice of this shabad

fork.setup: you're told your turn has come: this human life is your chance to meet the Lord. what does the shabad tell you to do?
options: join the company of the holy and remember the Name.
work harder at everything else first.
fork.reveal: Guru Arjan says other work can't do this job: meet with the sangat and meditate on the Name, now, while it's your turn.

original.note: Gurmukhi: maanukh, human; bhaee paraapat maanukh dehureeaa, you have received this human body.

trapdoor: what you thought: this human body is your chance is a motivational slogan.
what it means: a human life is the soul's turn, bareeaa, to meet the Lord, and it's happening now.
what a scholar hears: dehureeaa is glossed as an affectionate form of deh, body; the picture of a human birth as a rare turn appears elsewhere in gurbani too.

sources.ref: Asa M5, bhaee paraapat maanukh dehureeaa, Ang 12

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): the Harmandir Sahib line is now attributed to Sikh tradition; 'fallen at Your door' corrected to the text's 'sought Your shelter' (saran pare); trapdoor's sweeping claim about Guru Arjan's bani softened.

Shabad paraphrased: you have received this human body, this is your turn to meet Gobind; other works are of no use; join the saadhsangat, meditate on the Name alone; devote yourself to crossing the world ocean; life wasting in the love of maya; I haven't practiced jap, tap, sanjam, dharam; haven't served the holy or known the Lord King; Nanak: my deeds are lowly, I seek Your shelter, protect my honor. Confirm.
Dehureeaa as a diminutive of deh: confirm.
Guru Arjan 'oversaw the building of the Harmandir Sahib': confirm phrasing (construction began under Guru Arjan, c. 1588–1604).
